```{r setup}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(PKNCA)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Iwaki_2021_guselkumab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Iwaki_2021_guselkumab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.1953>
* PK model: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.1063> (Yao 2018; packaged as
  `Yao_2018_guselkumab`)

Iwaki 2021 describes the longitudinal Palmoplantar Pustulosis Area and
Severity Index (PPPASI) in Japanese patients with palmoplantar pustulosis
(PPP) treated with guselkumab or placebo. The analysis was sequential: the
population PK model of Yao 2018, developed in plaque psoriasis, was applied
to the PPP patients to obtain individual PK parameters, and those were then
held fixed while the PK/PD model was estimated. Iwaki 2021 reports no PK
estimates of its own, so the PK layer of this model is the Yao 2018 model
unchanged (one compartment, first-order SC absorption, body weight on CL/F
and V/F, diabetes and race on CL/F).

The PD layer follows the bounded-outcome-score approach of Hu et al. for the
PASI score. The PPPASI score (0 to 72 in 0.1-point steps) is mapped to
`k / 720` with `k = 0, ..., 720` and treated as an ordered categorical
variable with

$$P(\text{PPPASI} = k/10) = B\!\left(\tfrac{k+1}{721}\right) - B\!\left(\tfrac{k}{721}\right),$$

where `B` is the CDF of a beta distribution with mean `mu` and precision
`tau` (shape parameters `mu * tau` and `(1 - mu) * tau`). The mean is

$$\text{logit}(\mu) = \text{logit}(\mu_b) - P_{max}\left(1 - e^{-k_p t}\right) - DE\,(1 - R(t)) + k_{dspg}\,t,$$

with a type I indirect-response latent variable

$$\frac{dR}{dt} = k_{out}\left(1 - \frac{C_p}{IC_{50} + C_p}\right) - k_{out} R, \qquad R(0) = 1.$$

# Population

The analysis pooled a phase 2 proof-of-concept study (49 patients randomized
1:1 to guselkumab 200 mg or placebo SC at weeks 0 and 4, efficacy through
week 24) and a phase 3 confirmatory study (159 patients randomized 1:1:1 to
guselkumab 100 mg, 200 mg or placebo SC at weeks 0, 4 and 12 and then every
8 weeks, efficacy through week 52; the placebo group was rerandomized 1:1 to
100 or 200 mg at weeks 16 and 20, then every 8 weeks). Both were
double-blind, placebo-controlled trials at multiple sites in Japan.

The PK/PD dataset held 207 patients, all Japanese, with 160 women (77%) and
125 smokers (60%). Median baseline body weight was 59.7 kg (range 37.0 to
98.2) and median baseline PPPASI was 24.6 (range 4.8 to 59.4); 1813 PK and
2718 PPPASI observations were analysed (Iwaki 2021 Methods, "Clinical Study
Designs", and Results, "Exploratory Assessments of the Observed Data"). Age
is not reported. The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
readModelDb("Iwaki_2021_guselkumab")()$population[c(
  "n_subjects", "n_studies", "weight_median", "sex_female_pct",
  "race_ethnicity", "smoker_pct", "baseline_pppasi"
)]
```

collected here.

| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_vc` | 0.998, 0.829 | Yao 2018 Table 4 footnotes b and c |
| `e_diab_cl`, `e_race_cl` | 1.12, 1.11 | Yao 2018 Table 4 footnote b |
| `etalcl + etalvc`, `etalka` | 0.126736, 0.083133, 0.078400; 1.6641 | Yao 2018 Table 4 (IIV 35.6%, 28.0%, 129%; correlation 0.834) |

| PK structure and covariates | n/a | Iwaki 2021 Methods, "Population PK Modeling" |

# Virtual cohort

The observed data are not public. The cohort below follows the phase 3
design, the larger and longer of the two studies: guselkumab 100 mg or
200 mg at weeks 0, 4 and 12 and then every 8 weeks, and placebo at weeks 0,
4 and 12 followed by guselkumab 100 or 200 mg at weeks 16 and 20 and then
every 8 weeks, through week 52. Body weight is log-normal around the cohort
median of 59.7 kg, truncated to the observed range; every subject is
non-White (`RACE_WHITE = 0`) and non-diabetic (`DIS_DIAB = 0`, see
Assumptions).

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20211)
set.seed(20211)

n_per_arm <- 150L
wk <- 7

active_weeks <- c(0, 4, 12, 20, 28, 36, 44)
switch_weeks <- c(16, 20, 28, 36, 44)
arms <- tibble(
  treatment = c("Gus 100 mg", "Gus 200 mg", "Placebo -> Gus 100 mg", "Placebo -> Gus 200 mg"),
  dose_mg = c(100, 200, 100, 200),
  dose_weeks = list(active_weeks, active_weeks, switch_weeks, switch_weeks)
)

# Weekly grid for the score, plus a daily grid over the last dosing interval
# (weeks 44 to 52) for the steady-state NCA.
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 52 * wk, by = wk), seq(44 * wk, 52 * wk, by = 1))))

make_arm <- function(i, id_offset) {
  arm <- arms[i, ]
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  wt <- exp(rnorm(n_per_arm, log(59.7), 0.2))
  wt <- pmin(pmax(wt, 37.0), 98.2)
  covs <- tibble(id = ids, WT = wt, DIS_DIAB = 0L, RACE_WHITE = 0L)
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = arm$dose_weeks[[1]] * wk) |>
    mutate(amt = arm$dose_mg, cmt = "depot", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    left_join(covs, by = "id") |>
    mutate(treatment = arm$treatment)
}

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_arm(i, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

`rxSolve()` returns the beta mean `mu_pppasi` and the shape parameters
`alpha_pppasi` and `beta_pppasi` for every subject and visit. A PPPASI score
is drawn from the ordered categorical distribution by drawing `x` from the
beta distribution and taking `k = floor(721 * x)`, which falls in category
`k` with exactly the probability `B((k + 1)/721) - B(k/721)` of the model.
Given `mu`, visits are independent, as in the source model.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Iwaki_2021_guselkumab")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = c("treatment", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim <- sim |>
  mutate(
    pppasi = floor(721 * rbeta(n(), alpha_pppasi, beta_pppasi)) / 10,
    week = time / wk
  )

score <- sim |>
  filter(week == round(week)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  mutate(
    pppasi_bl = pppasi[week == 0],
    cfb = pppasi - pppasi_bl,
    pct_improve = 100 * (pppasi_bl - pppasi) / pppasi_bl
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

# Replicate published figures

## PPPASI change from baseline by arm (cf. Figure 2)

Figure 2 of Iwaki 2021 is a VPC of the change from baseline of the PPPASI
score by study and treatment group. The simulated median and 90% prediction
interval for the phase 3 design are shown below.

```{r figure-2}
score |>
  filter(week > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, week) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(cfb, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(cfb, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(cfb, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 16, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Week", y = "PPPASI change from baseline (points)",
    title = "Simulated PPPASI change from baseline, phase 3 design",
    caption = "Compare with Figure 2 of Iwaki 2021 (VPC). Dashed line: week 16 switch from placebo."
  )
```

## Change from baseline by baseline-severity quartile (Figure 3A)

```{r figure-3a}
bl_q <- score |>
  filter(week == 0, treatment %in% c("Gus 100 mg", "Gus 200 mg")) |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  mutate(bl_quartile = paste0("Q", dplyr::ntile(pppasi_bl, 4))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(id, bl_quartile)

score_q <- score |>
  inner_join(bl_q, by = "id")

score_q |>
  group_by(treatment, bl_quartile, week) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(cfb, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(cfb, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(cfb, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(week, Q50, colour = bl_quartile, fill = bl_quartile)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.10, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Week", y = "PPPASI change from baseline (points)",
    colour = "Baseline quartile", fill = "Baseline quartile",
    title = "Change from baseline by baseline PPPASI quartile",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3A of Iwaki 2021 (median and 90% prediction interval)."
  )
```

## Responder rates with 100 mg by baseline quartile (Figure 3B)

```{r figure-3b}
resp <- score_q |>
  filter(treatment == "Gus 100 mg", week > 0) |>
  group_by(bl_quartile, week) |>
  summarise(
    PPPASI50 = mean(pct_improve >= 50),
    PPPASI75 = mean(pct_improve >= 75),
    PPPASI90 = mean(pct_improve >= 90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("PPPASI"), names_to = "endpoint", values_to = "rate")

ggplot(resp, aes(week, 100 * rate, colour = bl_quartile)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  labs(
    x = "Week", y = "Responders (%)", colour = "Baseline quartile",
    title = "PPPASI50 / 75 / 90 responder rates, guselkumab 100 mg",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3B of Iwaki 2021."
  )
```

# Checks against the paper's statements

The paper reports its PD results graphically, so the checks below test the
statements it makes in the text.

**Baseline.** The typical baseline on the 0-1 scale is 0.356, i.e. about
25.6 points, against an observed median baseline of 24.6.

```{r check-baseline}
bl <- score |> filter(week == 0)
median(bl$pppasi)
stopifnot(abs(median(bl$pppasi) - 24.6) < 3)
```

**100 mg and 200 mg are almost identical.** With IC50 fixed at 1e-6 ug/mL,
`Cp / (IC50 + Cp)` is 1 for any measurable concentration, so the drug effect
does not depend on dose. The typical-value predictions for the two doses
coincide; the deterministic difference in the predicted mean score is
negligible.

```{r check-dose}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_events <- events |>
  filter(id %in% c(1L, n_per_arm + 1L)) |>
  mutate(WT = 59.7)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = typ_events, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(score_mean = 72 * mu_pppasi) |>
  select(treatment, time, score_mean) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = score_mean)
max_diff <- max(abs(typ[["Gus 100 mg"]] - typ[["Gus 200 mg"]]))
max_diff
stopifnot(max_diff < 0.01)
```

**Larger absolute but similar relative improvement at higher baseline.**
Figure 3A shows larger reductions in absolute points for patients with a
higher baseline score, while Figure 3B shows similar responder rates across
baseline quartiles.

```{r check-quartiles}
wk52 <- score_q |>
  filter(treatment == "Gus 100 mg", week == 52) |>
  group_by(bl_quartile) |>
  summarise(
    median_cfb = median(cfb),
    PPPASI50 = mean(pct_improve >= 50),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(wk52, digits = 2, caption = "Week 52, guselkumab 100 mg, by baseline quartile.")
q1 <- wk52$median_cfb[wk52$bl_quartile == "Q1"]
q4 <- wk52$median_cfb[wk52$bl_quartile == "Q4"]
# Absolute reductions differ several-fold between the extreme quartiles
# (Q4 roughly 3x Q1 here); the bound only requires Q4 to be the larger.
stopifnot(q4 < q1 - 5)
```

**Placebo response and worsening.** The placebo effect lowers the score
through week 16, and the disease-progression term, whose between-subject
variance is large, lets some placebo patients worsen.

```{r check-placebo}
plb16 <- score |>
  filter(grepl("^Placebo", treatment), week == 16)
c(
  median_cfb = median(plb16$cfb),
  pct_worse = 100 * mean(plb16$cfb > 0)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Iwaki 2021 gives one PK reference point: the IC50 sensitivity analysis fixed
IC50 at 1 ug/mL, "around the trough concentration of guselkumab under the
100-mg regimen". The steady-state NCA over the final dosing interval (weeks
44 to 52) is compared against that value for the 100 mg arm.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc), treatment %in% c("Gus 100 mg", "Gus 200 mg"),
         time >= 44 * wk) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1, treatment %in% c("Gus 100 mg", "Gus 200 mg")) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 44 * wk,
  end = 52 * wk,
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  cmin = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,   ~cmin,
  "Gus 100 mg", 1
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmin = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 50
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated steady-state trough (weeks 44 to 52) vs. the approximate value quoted in Iwaki 2021. * differs by more than 50%."
)

cmin_100 <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmin", treatment == "Gus 100 mg")
median(cmin_100$PPORRES)
stopifnot(median(cmin_100$PPORRES) > 0.5, median(cmin_100$PPORRES) < 2)
```

The simulated median trough with 100 mg every 8 weeks lies close to the
1 ug/mL the paper describes; the paper gives it only as an approximate
figure, so the comparison uses a wide tolerance.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **PK layer.** Iwaki 2021 used individual empirical Bayes PK parameters from
  the Yao 2018 model, which are not published. This model carries the Yao
  2018 population model (typical values, covariates, IIV and residual error)
  in their place, so simulated PK reflects the Yao 2018 variability applied
  to PPP covariates rather than the fitted PPP individuals.
- **Diabetes.** Iwaki 2021 does not report the prevalence of diabetes in the
  PPP cohort; the virtual cohort uses `DIS_DIAB = 0` for everyone.
- **Body weight.** Only the median and range are reported; weight is drawn
  log-normally (log-scale SD 0.2) around 59.7 kg and truncated to 37.0 to
  98.2 kg.
- **Time origin.** The placebo effect and disease progression use time since
  the first dose (study day), as the Supplemental `$ERROR` uses `TIME`.
- **Phase 2 arms** are not simulated; their shorter design (two doses,
  24 weeks) adds nothing the phase 3 arms do not already exercise.
- **Smoking** was tested on `kdspg` and not retained (Results), so it is not a
  covariate of the model.
- **Likelihood.** The ordered categorical beta likelihood of the source is
  encoded exactly with `ll(pppasi)`, using rxode2's regularized incomplete
  beta function `ibeta(a, b, x)` (equal to `pbeta(x, a, b)`), floored at
  `1e-30` as in the source. The score column supplied as `DV` must be the
  PPPASI score in points (0 to 72).

# Errata

- **Signs of the placebo and drug effects.** The Methods print
  `logit(mu) = logit(mu_b) + fp(t) + fd(t) + DSPG(t)`, with `fp` and `fd`
  both positive (Table 1: Fp = 1.55, DE = 2.97). The Supplemental NONMEM code
  subtracts both terms
  (`MuBlgt = BSlgt - PBMX * (1 - EXP(-PBRATE * TIME)) - DMX * (1 - F) + DSPG * TIME`).
  Only the subtracted form lowers the score on placebo and on guselkumab, as
  the paper reports, so the model follows the code.
- **Drug-effect variable.** The Supplemental `$ERROR` writes the drug effect
  as `DMX * (1 - F)`. On PPPASI records `F` is the amount in the third
  compartment, the latent variable `R(t)` (scale factor 1), which matches the
  Methods equation `fd(t) = DE [1 - R(t)]`.
- No correction notice for Iwaki 2021 was found on PubMed, Europe PMC or the
  publisher's page (checked 2026-10-23).
